newsitem.title: INDIA: Sliding world prices triggers Indian tin selling.
newsitem.headline: Sliding world prices triggers Indian tin selling.

text.p: Indian tin and nickel prices on Thursday extended losses while other base metals were steady in limited activity, dealers said.

Tin and nickel eased on increased arrivals of imported metals which slid overseas, triggering fresh selling. Tin moved down by 300 rupees at 30,200 rupees per quintal while nickel lost 200 rupees at 35,600 rupees per quintal.

"In the last three days, tin prices have crashed by 700 rupees and nickel prices by 600 rupees per quintal but I am expecting prices to go down further looking at the quiet physical activity," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay metal exchange.

Copper was steady at 13,925 rupees after losing 25 rupees on Wednesday, while zinc was quiet at 8,100 rupees. So was lead at 4,100 rupees amid nominal trading. Aluminium was quoted at the previous level of 7,700 rupees per quintal amid scattered trading.
